literal: Your letter says that wife, children, and elders are all in the Ministry of Justice, and you use this to coerce me, hoping I might return.
idiomatic: Your letter says my wife, children, and elders are all held by the Ministry of Justice, and that you mean to use them to force my return.

literal: Surely this shows a suspicious and narrow mind, not understanding the larger design.
idiomatic: This can only be the work of a suspicious and petty mind that does not grasp the larger design.

literal: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother lived and did not return;
idiomatic: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother was alive in Chu and would not return;

literal: the Dowager Empress was imprisoned in Chu yet begged for soup as calmly as ever.
idiomatic: the Dowager Empress was held prisoner in Chu yet asked for soup as calmly as ever.

literal: How much less should one fuss over wife and children!
idiomatic: How much less, then, should one make a fuss over wife and children!

literal: If you say killing them would help, you cannot stop wanting to; killing them would do you no good, yet you would still slaughter them. Your hostages are in your hands—what concern are they of mine?
idiomatic: If you think killing them would serve some purpose, you cannot restrain yourself; if it would do you no good, you would still butcher them anyway. Your hostages are in your hands—what is that to me?

literal: What Zundao said was not entirely empty, so I restate my case and speak again of heartfelt matters.
idiomatic: What Zundao reported was not wholly empty, and so I restate my case and speak again in earnest.

literal: Once I and the alliance leader were harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers set us apart, and we became enemies.
idiomatic: Once the alliance leader and I were as harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers came between us, and we became enemies.

literal: Touching the strings, grasping the arrow—I cannot but feel grief; torn silk returned in reply—how can words express it?
idiomatic: To touch the strings or grasp the arrow is to feel grief anew; to tear silk and send it back in reply—how can words say enough?

literal: When the Prince had read the letter, he asked who had written it.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng had read the letter, he asked who had written it.

literal: Someone said: "It was his Mobile Court Gentleman Wang Wei.
idiomatic: Someone said, "It was his mobile-court gentleman Wang Wei.

literal: " The Prince said: "With talent like this, why was I not told?
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "With talent like this, why was I not told?

literal: " The Prince wished to drive a wedge between Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally had Jing stir rebellion at Jingyang and planned with him to strike west; when Western Wei learned this, Jing turned instead to scheming with the south.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng wished to drive a wedge between Hou Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally sent Jing to stir rebellion at Jingyang and meant to plot the west together; when Western Wei learned of it, Jing turned instead to plotting with the south.

literal: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang people also did not believe it.
idiomatic: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang court did not believe it either.

literal: On renshen, the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with the Prince east of Ye, racing as if flying.
idiomatic: On renshen the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with Gao Cheng east of Ye, galloping as if in flight.

literal: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind: "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!
idiomatic: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind, "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!

literal: " Once, while attending him at drink, the Prince raised a great goblet and said: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink.
idiomatic: Once, while attending him at drink, Gao Cheng raised a great goblet and said, "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink.

literal: " The Eastern Wei emperor said displeased: "Since antiquity no state has failed to perish—why should I cling so to life!
idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor said, displeased, "Since antiquity no state has failed to perish—why should I cling so to life!

literal: " The Prince raged: "Imperial We!
idiomatic: Gao Cheng raged, "Imperial We!

literal: Imperial We!
idiomatic: Imperial We!

literal: Imperial We with dog's feet!
idiomatic: Dog-footed Imperial We!

literal: " He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes and went out.
idiomatic: He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes aside and stormed out.

literal: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.
idiomatic: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.

literal: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to the Prince, who told him to take one bolt.
idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to Gao Cheng, who told him to take one bolt.

literal: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said: "That too is only one bolt.
idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said, "That too is only one bolt.

literal: " Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.
idiomatic: Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.

literal: Born from river and sea, loyalty and righteousness move the noble heart.
idiomatic: Born from river and sea, loyalty and righteousness move the noble heart.

literal: " And he wept.
idiomatic: And he wept.

literal: On xinhai of the third month, the Prince went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang by way of Taihang from Luoyang.
idiomatic: On xinhai of the third month Gao Cheng went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang from Luoyang by way of the Taihang.

literal: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials as mutual admonition and encouragement.
idiomatic: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials, admonishing and encouraging them.

literal: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.
idiomatic: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.

literal: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking only talent regardless of occupation.
idiomatic: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and the brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking talent alone and not binding themselves to rank or trade.

literal: In the sixth month the Prince toured northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Cheng toured the northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.

literal: In the seventh month the Prince returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the seventh month Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang.

literal: On xinmao the Prince fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.
idiomatic: On xinmao Gao Cheng fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.

literal: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.
idiomatic: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, with the temple name Shizong.

literal: At the time a children's song ran: "A hundred-foot pole snaps; lamps lit beneath the water go out.
idiomatic: At the time a children's song ran, "A hundred-foot pole snaps; lamps lit beneath the water go out.

literal: " Those who understood took it as an omen that the Prince would die.
idiomatic: Those who understood took it as an omen that Gao Cheng would die.

literal: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate recited a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain.
idiomatic: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason recited before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain.

literal: " His voice was deeply mournful and tears would not stop; all who saw it found it strange.
idiomatic: His voice was deeply mournful and tears would not stop; all who saw it found it strange.

literal: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of Liang General Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; the Prince ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.
idiomatic: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of the Liang general Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; Gao Cheng ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.

literal: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; the Prince refused.
idiomatic: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; Gao Cheng refused.

literal: Jing appealed again; the Prince had kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said: "Complain again and you will be killed.
idiomatic: Jing appealed again; Gao Cheng had the kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said, "Complain again and you will be killed.

literal: " Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.
idiomatic: Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.

literal: At the time the Prince held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.
idiomatic: At the time Gao Cheng held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.

literal: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint; change would come within a month.
idiomatic: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint and that change would come within a month.

literal: The Prince said: "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me.

literal: " About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.
idiomatic: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.

literal: When Jing was about to bring food, the Prince held back and told the others: "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him.
idiomatic: When Jing was about to bring food, Gao Cheng held back and told the others, "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him.

literal: " Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.
idiomatic: Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.

literal: The Prince raged: "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!
idiomatic: Gao Cheng raged, "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!

literal: " Jing swung the knife and said: "I have come to kill you!
idiomatic: Jing swung the knife and said, "I have come to kill you!

literal: " The Prince threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.

literal: The assassins dragged him from the bed and so he was killed.
idiomatic: The assassins dragged him from the bed and killed him.

literal: Before this a rumor ran: "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.
idiomatic: Before this a rumor ran, "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.

literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
idiomatic: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

literal: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced: "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."
idiomatic: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced, "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
